## Vocabulary

Terms this pack was harvested with, grouped by their relation to the concept; counts are units matched / sources. Zero-hit terms are listed under Coverage. On every unit line, `keywords:` names the terms that matched.

- **self**: Salesforce event-alert observability and failure-injection tests (15/3)

## How it works

- [statement] Recommended timeout tests must distinguish exhausted demand from a healthy idle stream: when pending demand reaches zero the client must send another FetchRequest within 60 seconds; with pending demand and no events, the server sends an empty keepalive FetchResponse within 270 seconds. These are separate test conditions. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/references/methods/subscribe-rpc.html · keywords: Salesforce event-alert observability and failure-injection tests
- [statement] Recommended observability check: alert when scheduled synthetic-test telemetry disappears, as well as when a synthetic test fails. Salesforce Commerce engineering explicitly checks that test-tenant metrics exist during every continuous-test interval; applying that pattern to case alerts is a design recommendation, not a documented Pub/Sub feature. (low confidence) — https://engineering.salesforce.com/managing-availability-in-service-based-deployments-with-continuous-testing-61be968da4a/ · keywords: Salesforce event-alert observability and failure-injection tests

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] For Pub/Sub failure diagnostics, retain the gRPC status, the custom error code from trailers, and the RPC execution identifier. Salesforce documents the RPC identifier as useful for support investigations. (low confidence) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/guide/handling-errors.html · keywords: Salesforce event-alert observability and failure-injection tests
- [statement] Recommended failure-injection check: terminate a long-lived RPC and verify that the client starts a replacement call, limits retry attempts, and increases retry delays exponentially. Salesforce recommends bounded exponential backoff; a replacement RPC is required after the streaming connection fails. (medium confidence) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/guide/retry-rpc-calls.html · keywords: Salesforce event-alert observability and failure-injection tests · also: https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/guide/handling-errors.html
- [statement] Apex event tests use a separate test event bus and do not execute external Pub/Sub subscribers. Consequently, passing Apex tests alone cannot validate the external case-alert delivery path. (low confidence) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/platform-events/guide/platform-events-test-events.html · keywords: Salesforce event-alert observability and failure-injection tests
- [statement] The independent Wolverine Salesforce transport documents per-listener heartbeat counters for uptime, responses, events, errors, reconnects, and the last success or error. These provide a concrete implementation example for an alert collector dashboard. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12) — https://github.com/meyc-v1/wolverinefxcontrib-salesforcepubsub · keywords: Salesforce event-alert observability and failure-injection tests
- [statement] The Wolverine repository also documents crash/force-kill/restart and poison-message experiments. These are relevant failure-injection categories for an alert consumer; the repository’s observed outcomes apply to its transport and configuration, not to every Salesforce application. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12) — https://github.com/meyc-v1/wolverinefxcontrib-salesforcepubsub · keywords: Salesforce event-alert observability and failure-injection tests
- [statement] The Node Pub/Sub client exposes subscription callback signals for parsing/stream errors, stream end, keepalive, and stream status. Recommended instrumentation should distinguish those signals so a parsing failure is visible separately from a transport lifecycle change. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12) — https://github.com/pozil/pub-sub-api-node-client · keywords: Salesforce event-alert observability and failure-injection tests
- [statement] Poison-message test recommendation: inject an event parsing failure and verify that monitoring distinguishes it from a transport failure. The Node client documents both as possible error-callback causes. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12) — https://github.com/pozil/pub-sub-api-node-client · keywords: Salesforce event-alert observability and failure-injection tests

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Independent implementations provide practical local transport-test examples: Ballerina exercises unary and streaming gRPC using a self-signed TLS fixture, while OSO runs a local fake Salesforce without requiring an org. These are examples of fixture-based tests, rather than proof that a local fixture reproduces every production behavior. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12) — https://github.com/ballerina-platform/module-ballerinax-salesforce.pubsub · keywords: Salesforce event-alert observability and failure-injection tests · also: https://github.com/osodevops/kafka-connect-salesforce-oss/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
- [statement] OSO documents a local fake Salesforce harness with an in-process Pub/Sub gRPC implementation supporting replay semantics. It is a concrete external-client test-harness lead, rather than evidence that this case-alert application has passed integration tests. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12) — https://github.com/osodevops/kafka-connect-salesforce-oss · keywords: Salesforce event-alert observability and failure-injection tests

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Ballerina maintains a separate live shared-org suite that is disabled by default. A successful local fixture run therefore does not by itself establish that the live sandbox suite ran. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12) — https://github.com/ballerina-platform/module-ballerinax-salesforce.pubsub · keywords: Salesforce event-alert observability and failure-injection tests
- [statement] Idle-stream test: while delivery demand remains outstanding and no events are available, expect an empty response as a keepalive within 270 seconds. Treat idle health separately from event-arrival activity. (low confidence) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/references/methods/subscribe-rpc.html · keywords: Salesforce event-alert observability and failure-injection tests
- [statement] Request-starvation test: after the requested batch is exhausted, verify that the client renews demand within 60 seconds. Salesforce specifies this deadline for keeping the subscription alive. (low confidence) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/references/methods/subscribe-rpc.html · keywords: Salesforce event-alert observability and failure-injection tests
- [statement] OSO requires behavioral changes to have coverage against its fake harness and documents a build check with additional Docker end-to-end tests in CI. This is a useful model for layered client validation. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12) — https://github.com/osodevops/kafka-connect-salesforce-oss/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md · keywords: Salesforce event-alert observability and failure-injection tests

## Research summary — Salesforce event-alert observability and failure-injection tests

Reliable case-alert operation needs observable RPC failures and tests that exercise both broken streams and healthy idle periods. The evidence supports capturing diagnostic identifiers, bounded retry checks, demand-aware timeout tests, and synthetic-test monitoring. Independent connector implementations demonstrate local gRPC fixtures and operational counters; live sandbox checks remain a separate layer. Apex event tests do not run external Pub/Sub consumers. The proposed acceptance tests are design recommendations derived from these sources. Community transport experiments illustrate fault categories without establishing universal delivery guarantees.
